```{ojs}
//| echo: false
bundle = FileAttachment("data/latest.json").json()
status = FileAttachment("data/status.json").json()
targets = bundle.targets ?? []
headline = targets[0]
formatMonth = (value) => value ? new Date(`${value}T00:00:00`).toLocaleDateString("en-US", {month: "long", year: "numeric"}) : "Pending"
formatFeet = (value) => Number.isFinite(value) ? `${value.toLocaleString("en-US", {minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2})} ft` : "Not available"
formatValue = (value) => Number.isFinite(value) ? value.toFixed(3) : "Not used"
formatContribution = (value) => Number.isFinite(value) ? `${value >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${value.toFixed(3)} ft` : "Not available"
stale = status.attempted_issue && bundle.issue && status.attempted_issue !== bundle.issue
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
headlineView = headline ? html`<section class="headline-band">
  <div>
    <p class="eyebrow">${formatMonth(headline.month)} monthly mean</p>
    <p class="headline-number">${formatFeet(headline.pred)}</p>
    <p class="range">Nominal 90% interval ${formatFeet(headline.q05)}–${formatFeet(headline.q95)}</p>
  </div>
  <dl class="issue-facts">
    <div><dt>Issued</dt><dd>${bundle.issue}</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Status</dt><dd>${bundle.issue_status ?? "experimental"}</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Version</dt><dd>${bundle.forecast_version ?? "unknown"}</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Model</dt><dd>${bundle.headline_model}</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Data through</dt><dd>${status.data_max ?? "Pending"}</dd></div>
  </dl>
</section>` : html`<section class="headline-band pending">
  <div><p class="eyebrow">Next monthly mean</p><p class="headline-number">Pending</p>
  <p class="range">No complete headline issue is available.</p></div>
</section>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
staleNotice = stale
  ? html`<div class="data-notice" role="status">The latest run had incomplete inputs. This page retains the complete issue from ${bundle.issue}.</div>`
  : html``
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Research prototype"}
This forecast is experimental. It has not been validated for operational use. In repeatedly used development data, the headline model’s mean absolute error is 0.13, 0.33, and 0.58 ft. These values apply at leads 1, 3, and 6. Persistence errors are 0.34, 0.90, and 1.33 ft. At lead 24, the headline model is worse than persistence: 1.92 versus 1.79 ft. These results come from 157 overlapping monthly cutoffs, or about 13 water years, rather than an independent test.
:::

## Purpose and scope

This page reports a dated forecast of the calendar-month mean water-surface elevation of the Great Salt Lake’s south arm. The measurement comes from USGS gauge 10010000 at Saltair Boat Harbor. Elevation is in feet above the National Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929 (NGVD 29); it is not the lake’s depth.

The forecast uses data through the last complete calendar month and covers the next 24 monthly means. Lead 1 is the issue month. Lead 24 is 23 calendar months after the issue date. The main evidence supports use as a short-range research forecast. It does not support a claim of 24-month skill over persistence.

## Forecast path

The dark line shows observed monthly means. The colored line shows the headline point forecast. The band is a nominal central 90% interval calibrated from retrospective errors for the same lead and issue season. The point forecast is estimated separately and need not equal the interval median.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
history = (bundle.observations ?? []).map(d => ({...d, month: new Date(`${d.month}T00:00:00`)}))
path = targets.map(d => ({...d, month: new Date(`${d.month}T00:00:00`)}))
forecastPlot = path.length ? Plot.plot({
  height: 410,
  marginLeft: 72,
  marginBottom: 44,
  x: {label: null, grid: false},
  y: {label: "Elevation (ft NGVD 29)", grid: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.areaY(path, {x: "month", y1: "q05", y2: "q95", fill: "#98c9cb", fillOpacity: 0.42}),
    Plot.lineY(history, {x: "month", y: "elevation", stroke: "#202a27", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.lineY(path, {x: "month", y: "pred", stroke: "#087f8c", strokeWidth: 3}),
    Plot.dot(path.slice(0, 1), {x: "month", y: "pred", fill: "#c84a3d", r: 5})
  ]
}) : html`<p class="empty-state">Forecast data will appear after a complete issue.</p>`
```

### How to interpret the interval

The interval is marginal, not a set of simulated lake trajectories. It gives a separate range for each lead. It does not give the entire path a 90% chance of staying inside the band. It also gives no probability for the spring maximum or the date of a minimum.

In development evaluation, the nominal 90% interval contains 87% of observations at leads 6 and 12 in aggregate. Lead-6 coverage varies by issue season, from 77% for April–June issues to 92% for July–October issues. Historical evaluation also uses revised source data rather than the exact values available on each past issue date.

## Model inputs

The chart decomposes the selected point forecast into the terms of the fitted covariate model. The reference path is the fitted value when its inputs equal their training means. Each bar is the fitted contribution from the current input’s difference from that mean. The reference path and all bars sum to the point forecast.

These contributions describe the regression. They do not show cause and effect because the inputs vary together and the data are observational.

The inputs are:

- Current lake elevation: the south-arm monthly mean in the last complete month.
- Snow water equivalent: the depth of liquid water stored in mountain snowpack, in inches.
- Water-year precipitation: rain and snow measured since October 1 at the same mountain sites, in inches.
- Difference between the arms: south-arm elevation minus north-arm elevation, in feet.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
targetOptions = targets.length ? targets.map(d => ({label: formatMonth(d.month), value: d.h})) : [{label: "Pending", value: 1}]
viewof selectedH = Inputs.select(targetOptions, {label: "Target month", format: d => d.label, value: targetOptions[0]})
selectedLead = selectedH.value
selected = targets.find(d => d.h === selectedLead)
labels = ({
  avg_elevation: "Current lake elevation",
  swe_eom_gsl: "Snow water equivalent",
  prec_wy_eom_gsl: "Water-year precipitation",
  head_diff_ft: "Difference between the arms"
})
drivers = (selected?.contributions ?? [])
  .filter(d => d.input !== "reference_path")
  .map(d => ({...d, label: labels[d.input] ?? d.input}))
reference = (selected?.contributions ?? []).find(d => d.input === "reference_path")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
driverSummary = selected ? html`<div class="target-summary">
  <span>${formatFeet(selected.pred)} point forecast</span>
  <span>${Math.round((selected.covariate_weight ?? selected.snow_weight ?? 0) * 100)}% covariate-model weight</span>
  <span>${formatFeet(reference?.contribution_ft)} reference path</span>
</div>` : html``
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
driverPlot = drivers.length ? Plot.plot({
  height: 260,
  marginLeft: 170,
  marginBottom: 42,
  x: {label: "Contribution to elevation (ft)", grid: true},
  y: {label: null, domain: drivers.map(d => d.label)},
  color: {domain: ["Lower", "Raise"], range: ["#c84a3d", "#087f8c"], legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(drivers, {x: "contribution_ft", y: "label", fill: d => d.contribution_ft < 0 ? "Lower" : "Raise", tip: true}),
    Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "#202a27"})
  ]
}) : html`<p class="empty-state">Input contributions will appear after a complete issue.</p>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
driverDetails = drivers.length ? html`<dl class="driver-values">
  ${drivers.map(d => html`<div>
    <dt>${d.label}</dt>
    <dd class="driver-contribution">${formatContribution(d.contribution_ft)}</dd>
    <dd>Current ${formatValue(d.value)}; training mean ${formatValue(d.reference)}</dd>
  </div>`)}
</dl>` : html``
```

## Model comparison

The headline `blend` combines a snowpack regression with a damped seasonal time-series model. The issue also exports simpler models for comparison. `naive_last`, which repeats the last monthly mean, is the persistence benchmark. The headline model is not the best development candidate at every lead, and the table should not be read as a ranking of validated products.

The values below are point forecasts in feet NGVD 29 at 3, 6, 12, and 24 monthly steps from the last observed month.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
modelLeads = [3, 6, 12, 24]
modelRows = d3.groups(bundle.models ?? [], d => d.model)
  .map(([model, rows]) => ({model, ...Object.fromEntries(rows.map(r => [`h${r.h}`, r.pred]))}))
  .sort((a, b) => d3.ascending(a.model, b.model))
modelTable = modelRows.length ? Inputs.table(modelRows, {
  columns: ["model", ...modelLeads.map(h => `h${h}`)],
  header: Object.fromEntries([["model", "Model"], ...modelLeads.map(h => [`h${h}`, `Lead ${h}`])]),
  format: Object.fromEntries(modelLeads.map(h => [`h${h}`, v => Number.isFinite(v) ? v.toFixed(2) : "—"])),
  rows: 20
}) : html`<p class="empty-state compact">Model comparisons will appear after a complete issue.</p>`
```

## Data and provenance

Forecast accuracy depends on the age and completeness of the inputs. The issue records its last complete month and the number of daily gauge readings. It also records the SNOTEL site count and any required covariates missing at the cutoff.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
vintage = bundle.vintage ?? {}
vintageView = html`<dl class="driver-values">
  <div><dt>Last complete month</dt><dd>${vintage.data_max ?? "Pending"}</dd></div>
  <div><dt>Daily gauge readings</dt><dd>${vintage.observation_count ?? "Pending"}</dd></div>
  <div><dt>SNOTEL sites recorded</dt><dd>${vintage.n_snotel_sites ?? "Pending"}</dd></div>
  <div><dt>Missing required covariates</dt><dd>${(vintage.missing_covariates ?? []).length ? vintage.missing_covariates.join(", ") : "none"}</dd></div>
</dl>`
```

Each dated issue has a write-once CSV and metadata sidecar. A complete headline issue also has an explanation sidecar. The current export code records the issue status, model version, code state, data and configuration hashes, input support, and interval calibration. Older issues can predate some fields.

Read [Method and evidence](methodology.qmd) for the equations, source timing, evaluation design, limitations, code links, and primary data sources. The [dated forecast record](https://github.com/jcblsn/gsl-forecast/tree/main/forecasts) is available with the source code.
